s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis
salient_findings: Recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb
key_facts: 56-year-old man
Four-year history of skin lesion on the right thumb
Partial amputation of the thumb in December 2016
Lesion reappeared in August 2017
No significant medical history
No medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb stump
Lesion is mobile over deep structures
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node on metastatic workup
CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis and bone scan performed

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesion on the thumb with potential for metastasis

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesion with possible local invasion

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer with potential for metastasis

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer with possible local recurrence

raw.rationale: The lesion's recurrence after partial amputation and the presence of an enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node suggest an aggressive skin cancer, which is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma than the other options.

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: While possible, melanoma is less likely given the lack of specific mention of pigmentation or other characteristic features of melanoma.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: This is a rare skin cancer that typically has a longer history and a distinctive appearance, not clearly described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a highly aggressive cancer, but it is very rare and typically presents in older adults with significant sun exposure or immunosuppression, not clearly indicated here.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While common, basal cell carcinoma is less likely to metastasize and recur aggressively as described, especially with lymph node involvement.
